newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Repiublic - March 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Repiublic - March 28.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik came under attack in parliament yesterday by members of the opposition who criticised the government's economic policies. Kocarnik was being blamed for the country's budget deficit which at the end of the first quarter is approaching eight billion crowns.

- Shareholders of the Kaucuk Group and Chemapol Group voted yesterday to allow the two companies to merge with the state-owned petrochemical holding company, Unipetrol. The goal of the merger is to amass capital of the petrochemical giants and form one holding company.

- The lumber and pulp and paper industries are still bogged down in a recession, following a relative period of prosperity between 1993-95. Reasons for the slump include a recession being experienced by pulp manufacturers, high export levels of lumber, low worker productivity and underutilised capacities of mills. Some mills are being shutdown as a result.

MLADA FRONTA DNES - Only a letter from the health minister stands between the Association of Pharmaceutical Distributors and their goal of forcing hospitals who are not paying for medication to be put up for sale. The association agreed yesterday to a plan whereby the health ministry would provide a loan to health insurance companies so they can pay-off debts to hospitals, which in urn could settle debts with the pharmaceutical distributors.

- The stagnating residential real estate market received a much-needed boost when the government announced rent deregulation. Many people are now seeking to exchange larger flats for smaller living quarters, and apartment buildings previously considered to be unattractive are now being put up for sale.

- Shareholders of the two largest banking institutions in the country, Komercni banka and Ceska sporitelna can look forward to higher dividends this year. Questions continue to surround whether shareholders of the third largest bank, Investicni a Postovni banka will enjoy the same benefits, as the bank has delayed issuing its financial results.

LIDOVE NOVINY - Premier Vaclav Klaus downplayed concerns that the country's economy is in trouble. Klaus said that the government is carefully monitoring economic developments and is preparing special measures to cope with any problems. The Premier also pointed to growth of the GDP during the final quarter of 1996 as an indicator that the economy is not suffering.
- The Czech National Bank warned against unchecked wage increases. According to bank spokesman Martin Svehla rising wages are the main cause behind the growing gap between domestic supply and demand.

PRAVO - Stanislav Gross of the Social Democrats said that the party should also support interests of the middle class in the country. Gross defined members of the middle class as being people who are able to financially support themselves, live decent lives and not rely on social benefits from the state. Gross claims that his party has noted that increasingly more individuals who are educated and should fall into this category are applying for social benefits.
